name: How to Compare Interior Painting Bids

mainEntity.name: How do I compare bids for interior painting without missing hidden prep costs?
mainEntity.text: How do I compare bids for interior painting without missing hidden prep costs?

acceptedAnswer.text: To compare interior painting bids accurately, focus on scope rather than just price. Two bids can look similar but include very different prep, materials, and finish levels. Check whether the contractor is patching holes, sanding, caulking, spot-priming stains, applying full primer where needed, and including one or two finish coats. Ask whether paint is included, whether furniture moving is included, and whether trim, ceilings, closets, or doors are part of the job. In occupied homes, also ask about dust control and daily cleanup. Hidden costs often appear when the estimate is vague about surface condition or excludes repairs that are necessary for a quality finish. The best bid is usually the one that defines the work most clearly.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare painting bids by checking surface prep, primer use, number of coats, repairs, masking, cleanup, and whether materials are included. The cheapest bid often leaves out patching or primer, which raises the true cost later. A clear bid should show exactly what is being painted and what condition the surfaces must be in before work starts.
